sana-sec: Security advisory — PII/credentials may have been shared via support tickets. We found multiple presigned S3 URLs and a DB connection string pasted into a Zendesk ticket thread for a partner onboarding. Immediate actions below.

mike-support: Ack, which tickets? can you share ticket ids?

sana-sec: Ticket IDs: ZD-4821, ZD-4829. Example excerpt (redacted): ```SupportAgent: here's the debug bundle https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-prod-dumps/2026-03-20/trace.tar.gz?AWSAccessKeyId=AKIA...&Expires=1700000000&Signature=xyz``` The presigned URLs grant GET access to backups containing log files with potential tokens and user emails. Also found a JDBC URL: ```jdbc:postgresql://db.prod.internal:5432/appdb?user=svc_user&password=secret123``` in ticket ZD-4829 paste.

sec-bot: Automated scan of ticket attachments flagged 2 tickets with patterns matching presigned URL query params and 1 ticket with credential-like JDBC patterns. Incident id: sec-2026-046.

olivia-custops: The partner asked us to upload logs; support copied the file link into the ticket. We removed attachments when flagged but links were already visible.

jules-sre: Containment: I'll invalidate the presigned URLs by rotating the bucket policy and immediately rotating the S3 key used to generate them. Also toggling object ACLs to private and forcing a new presigned signer. ETA 15m.

it-ops: We'll block public access to the affected object prefixes and add a temporary deny for presigned URL generation from the support service identity.

sana-sec: Action items for teams: 1) Revoke any credentials found in the affected archives (DB creds, API keys). 2) Rotate S3 access keys used by support/upload services. 3) Run a grep on your repos and docs for exposed presigned URL patterns or plaintext JDBC strings.

mike-support: We'll search Zendesk for outbound links and run a purge for any ticket bodies containing "s3.amazonaws.com" or query params AWSAccessKeyId/Signature. Also updating agent guide to never paste presigned URLs into ticket body; use secure ticket attachments instead.

jules-sre: Forensics: downloading the object list for the presigned keys to see what was exposed. Running checksum and contents inventory. If you maintain any local copies from sharing with partner, assume compromise and rotate.

sana-sec: Priority timeline: 1) invalidate URLs & rotate keys (now), 2) identify exposed secrets and rotate high-risk credentials (4h), 3) conduct ticket audit for last 30 days (24h). If you interacted with those archives, mark host for scan.

it-ops: Adding new policy: disable inline presigned URL generation from non-prod support runners and require uploads to go through the secure upload service which returns a ticket-scoped ID, not a raw S3 link. We'll target rollout in 48h.

mike-support: Notifying impacted partner contacts and sending an advisory template. Also creating a quick-playbook for agents about redaction and how to request secure uploads.

sec-bot: Incident sec-2026-046 update: presigned URLs invalidated (2140012402). 2 tickets sanitized and attachments removed (2140012460). 1 DB credential marked high-risk and rotated (2140012605).

sana-sec: Please do not paste any secrets in ticket bodies. Use the secure upload flow and tag incidents in the tracker. If you find any more tickets with credential patterns, ping #eng-security and escalate to @sana-sec. We'll publish a post-incident summary after the audit. :lock:
